pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost because Cincinnati led early, Burrow fed Higgins (listed 59, 95, 90 on 302 air yards) and Chase against whatever JAX corners actually played (Brown and Braswell were both questionable this morning), and Jacksonville stopped handing Tuten the ball. Rodriguez's 20 carries became 12, Tuten finished in the 40s, and Washington repeated the listed 40-yard floor once a safety who did play sat on the deep shot. The other loss path is that the read was right and the unpriced Washington number was a tax. That counter-case gets stronger if the unsaved spread has Cincinnati laying a big number.
slip_story: One story only: Cincinnati's defense is soft on the ground and thin at safety and it does not blitz, which is how this Jacksonville offense has been good. Tuten rush over is the anchor; Washington rec over is the deep-shot correlate. They belong together only in a competitive game. They split in either blowout flip, so this is not a run-clock stack and not a shootout stack. Do not add a game under, do not add touchdowns, and do not add a second market on either player. Chase Brown rush+rec under 85 (listed 78, 82, 69 vs a 3.79 YPC JAX run defense) was considered and left off: no price, and JAX's 32% blitz is exactly the checkdown path that can push 66 rush plus a 22-yard receiving game over 85.
